classification.class: invalid read in bigint right shift due to missing zero-operand guard

bug_description.original: A NULL/uninitialized-pointer dereference (segmentation fault) in urshift (mrbgems/mruby-bigint/core/bigint.c). urshift does not correctly handle zero-valued mpz_t operands and can read from an invalid/garbage limb pointer when performing right-shift operations (observed via mpz_div_2exp -> mrb_bint_rshift). This leads to a crash (invalid memory read) and can be triggered by crafted inputs, causing denial-of-service or other undefined behavior in mruby.
bug_description.normalized: The parser accepts attacker-controlled Ruby source that is compiled and executed until the reproduced stack enters `int_rshift -> mrb_bint_rshift -> mpz_div_2exp -> urshift`. In vulnerable `urshift`, the only early return is `if (n == 0)`, so the function does not handle a numerically zero bigint operand before entering the limb-processing branch. The upstream patch adds `else if (uzero(a)) { mpz_set_int(mrb, c1, 0); }`, showing the missing safety obligation. Without that guard, `urshift` dereferences `a->p[i]` in the shift loop and ASan reports the invalid read at line 374.

source.description: The project parser stores the attacker-controlled Ruby source buffer and its length as the parser input that will be compiled and executed.
source.value_from: attacker-controlled Ruby program text produced from the saved fuzz testcase

root_cause.description: `urshift` only guards the no-op shift count and omits the required zero-operand check `uzero(a)` before reading limbs from `a`.

sink.description: `urshift` consumes the unchecked operand state by reading `a->p[i]` inside the limb-shift loop, matching the ASan crash at line 374.

tainted_value_origin.description: Attacker-controlled Ruby source bytes become the parser input string used to build and execute the program that reaches bigint right shift.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: saved testcase text fed to mruby's project parser

fine_trace.note: The project parser stores the attacker-controlled Ruby source buffer that will be compiled and later executed by mruby.
After parsing, mruby executes the compiled program. The saved crash stack shows this execution reaches the numeric right-shift helper rather than stopping earlier in the parser.
On the reproduced run, execution enters `int_rshift` and takes the bigint-specific branch; this is established by the saved crash stack frame that continues into `mrb_bint_rshift`.
The bigint right-shift path forwards the source bigint `b->mp` and shift width into `mpz_div_2exp`, which the reproduced stack places immediately before `urshift`.
When `mpz_div_2exp` reaches `urshift` with a nonzero intra-limb shift, `urshift` checks only `n == 0` and has no `uzero(a)` fast path. The fix adds that missing zero-operand guard before the loop.
Because the nonzero-shift branch proceeds without a zero-operand check, the loop reads `a->p[i]`; ASan reports the fatal invalid read at this exact statement.

poc.trigger: The saved testcase is an accepted fuzz input whose compiled execution reaches `int_rshift -> mrb_bint_rshift -> mpz_div_2exp -> urshift` on the vulnerable commit and crashes at `urshift` line 374 under ASan.

format.name: protobuf-derived Ruby source text consumed by mruby parser
format.contract: An input accepted by mruby's parser and executed to the bigint right-shift path so that `mrb_bint_rshift` calls `mpz_div_2exp`, which then reaches `urshift` with `n != 0`; on the vulnerable build, `urshift` lacks the `uzero(a)` guard added by the patch and crashes on the read at line 374.
